title: kv-cache-corruption-sampling-and-playbook-draft
content:
Summary:

This is a working draft incident review + runbook fragment for a class of production incidents observed in Oct-Nov 2024 where a subtle KV cache corruption combined with continuous-batching backlog produced intermittent OOMs and, in one case, a batch-assembler deadlock that required manual intervention. This doc captures the reproduction notes, triage timeline, temporary mitigations used on-call, and proposed durable runbook steps and long-term fixes.

High-level impact:
- Affects serving-runtime processes on Dedicated and Private clusters that use the new incremental-kv-rewrite codepath (launched July 2024).
- Symptoms: elevated memory usage on a subset of replicas, repeated cache rehydration attempts, inflight request queue growth, eventual OOM in the accelerator proxy or python worker, and in ~2% of crashes the batch assembler thread pool stops making forward progress (deadlock).
- Customer-visible: 1.2% P90 latency spikes for affected routes, 0.3% request error rate increase over a 3-hour window during the largest incident. No data loss reported, but failover and degraded latency.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
- Two concurrent bugs interacting: (1) an undercount in the async-kv-prefetch accounting logic that sometimes reports a smaller cache size than reality after partial writes, which causes a periodic aggressive rehydration (duplicate entries + oversized shards) and (2) a race in continuous-batching where a drained batch slot is requeued while the KV iterator is in an inconsistent state, producing a circular wait across batch locks and the cache eviction mutex -> deadlock. The combination amplifies memory pressure (duplicate objects) leading to OOM.

Evidence collected:
- Core dumps and heap profiles (pprof) from three host machines show duplicated large Tensor buffers with similar allocation stacks (stack frames point to kv_rehydrate_worker::insert and incremental_rewrite::commit).
- Logs show repeated "kv:rehydrate:shard X started" then later "kv:rehydrate:shard X aborted: inconsistent-length" followed by immediate restart within <200ms.
- Metrics: kv_shard_rehydrates_total spiked by 10x; kv_estimated_bytes and kv_actual_bytes diverged by ~25% during incidents.
- Traces from distributed tracing show request A waiting on batch-assembler lock L1 while request B holds L1 waiting on kv-evict lock L2; B waits on I/O that is blocked by the rehydrate loop -> circular.
- Repro script in staging (see linked PR) reproduces memory amplification at scale for specific model sizes and sequence lengths.

Immediate on-call playbook (what was done during incidents):
1) Detect:
   - Alert: "serving-runtime.kv.rehydrate.rate > 50/min and node_mem_rss_percent > 85%" fired.
   - On-call engineer verified via dashboards (kv_rehydrate_rate, kv_size_mismatch_ratio, batch_queue_length).
2) Short-term mitigation steps executed:
   - Set cluster feature-flag incremental_kv_rewrite=false via feature rollouts API (rollback) to stop new rehydrate cycles. (Command: curl -X POST $FEATURE_API -d '{"flag":"incremental_kv_rewrite","value":false}')
   - Scaled up node autoscaler policy to add +10% buffer for 30min to reduce OOM flapping.
   - For deadlocked replicas we executed: kill -SIGQUIT <pid> on the affected serving-runtime process to trigger graceful metrics dump and restart.
   - Enabled temporary circuit-breaker for the slow route (per-route rate limit) to reduce inflight concurrency while we investigate.
3) Customer comms and throttling:
   - Applied per-customer route throttle for largest customers to limit amplification; notified CS and affected customers via post-incident Slack thread.

Proposed durable runbook (draft):
This is intended to be added into the SRE runbook library under "serving-runtime/kv-cache". Steps are ordered from detection to resolution, with clear escalation points.

Detection rules (monitoring):
- ALERT if kv_shard_rehydrates_total > baseline * 6 over 5m AND kv_size_mismatch_ratio > 0.1
- ALERT if node_mem_rss_percent > 85% for >2m on >3 nodes in same AZ
- ALERT if batch_queue_length > 500 for >1m and average batch_wait_time > 50ms
Mitigation steps (run):
A. Immediate action (on-call engineer):
  1. Toggle feature-flag incremental_kv_rewrite=false for affected clusters (fast rollback).
  2. Throttle routes: apply per-route concurrency cap 25% below normal to shed load.
  3. If mem pressure persists: trigger node autoscaler emergency_scale(+15% for 1 hour).
  4. If replica is unresponsive and batch_queue_length stagnant -> restart process gracefully, capture core and metrics (systemd-coredump or gcore).
B. If deadlock suspected (batch assembler not progressing):
  1. Run diagnostic: curl http://localhost:9000/debug/locks to fetch lock table snapshot.
  2. If circular wait lines present, run kill -SIGUSR1 to dump thread stacks, upload to /tmp/incident-<ts>-stacks.txt, then restart the process.
  3. Escalate to eng-serving-runtime oncall (pager) if more than 2 replicas show deadlock in 15 minutes.
C. Recovery coordination:
  1. After actions, monitor kv_rehydrate_rate, kv_size_mismatch_ratio, and heap growth for 30 minutes.
  2. Re-enable feature-flag only under a canary rollout (5% traffic) with elevated tracing and heap sampling.

Long-term fixes (engineering tickets):
- INF-1427: Fix undercount in async-kv-prefetch accounting (owner: Connor). Priority: P0 for Dedicated/private clusters.
- INF-1463: Remove non-transactional partial writes from incremental_rewrite; add two-phase commit for shard replacements (owner: Anaïs). Priority: P1.
- INF-1481: Harden continuous-batching lock ordering and add lock-timeout detection that triggers watchdog to break circular waits (owner: Diego). Priority: P0.
- INF-1510: Add end-to-end chaos test in CI that simulates rehydrate aborts and verifies no memory amplification.

Regression guardrails and post-release checks:
- Add unit tests for shard accounting and invariants (expected bytes vs actual after partial-write failure).
- Add e2e perf test that runs incremental_kv_rewrite under interleaved failures and asserts max memory amplification < 1.5x.
- Dashboard: new panel comparing kv_estimated_bytes / kv_actual_bytes, and a guard alert if ratio < 0.9 or > 1.1.

Runbook TODOs and open questions (draft notes):
- Do we want to maintain a hot-fix branch that can be cherry-picked and shipped to Private customers faster? (ops + eng alignment needed)
- Which teams own cluster feature-flags? Add them to the on-call rotation playbook for faster toggles.
- Decide on automated soft-restart strategy if a single replica exhibits > 3 untriggered rehydrates within 10 minutes.

Appendix: diagnostic commands and helpful snippets
- Fetch lock table snapshot:
  curl -sS http://localhost:9000/debug/locks | jq '.' > /tmp/locks-$(date +%s).json
- Dump heap profile (python worker):
  kill -USR1 <pid>  # configured handler writes /tmp/heap-<pid>.pprof
- Trigger controlled rollback of feature flag:
  curl -X POST $FEATURE_API -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"incremental_kv_rewrite","value":false,"scope":"cluster:prod-us-west2"}'
- Example log snippet that was useful: 
  2024-10-28T02:12:03Z [info] kv:rehydrate:shard=7 started src=node-45
  2024-10-28T02:12:03Z [warn] kv:rehydrate:shard=7 aborted reason=inconsistent-length
  2024-10-28T02:12:03Z [info] kv:rehydrate:shard=7 restarted (attempt=2)

Ownership and next steps:
- Owners for immediate fixes: Connor Liu (INF-1427), Diego Ramirez (INF-1481).
- Schedule 2-week hardening sprint with SRE and serving-runtime teams to complete P0 tickets and add CI chaos tests.
- Add this doc to Confluence under "SRE Runbooks / serving-runtime" and link to INF tickets (owner: Maya).

Notes about uniqueness and intended audience:
- This doc is intentionally operational and terse. It is meant for SREs and oncall engineers who will act during incidents, and for serving-runtime engineers planning fixes. It is not the formal postmortem — a separate long-form postmortem will be produced after full RCA.

-- End of draft --
